sections.html:
Wentzville sits in western St. Charles County. The city counted 44,372 people in 2020 and now has about 49,495, up from 29,070 in 2010. That growth shows in the housing: owners live in 82.5% of homes, the median owner-reported home value is $331,300, median rent is $1,345, and median household income is $112,394. The average commute is 27.8 minutes, so many buyers are weighing the drive to St. Louis jobs.

The city asks nothing of you in the way of an occupancy inspection when you sell. The rules change only if the buyer plans to rent the house out. The rest of this page covers that inspection, the fees a buyer will ask about, how the county tax bill works, and what to line up before you list.

No inspection is required for an ordinary sale. Wentzville requires one only when a house will be leased, and it has to pass before a tenant moves in. If you sell to a buyer who plans to live there, the city is not involved in the closing.

  • The residential occupancy inspection costs $50 and stays valid for 90 days.
  • Request it through the city's SmartGov permit portal. Once the fee is paid, scheduling normally takes one to two business days.
  • A new inspection is needed each time the resident changes at a property.
  • A buyer of new construction does not need one, because the builder gets occupancy with the construction permit.

For questions, the Building Division answers at (636) 327-5101, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. If your buyer is an investor who will rent the place out, mention the 90-day window early so a tenant's move-in date is not held up.

sections.h2: City and county fees at a glance
sections.html:
These are the dollar figures a buyer or tenant is most likely to ask about.

Fees tied to a Wentzville house
FeeAmountWhen it applies
Residential occupancy inspection$50Rental or lease, valid 90 days
Water, trash and sewer account deposit$150New service at the address
Partial property tax paymentFrom $20Paid to the county Collector
E-check payment of tax$1.50Online or by phone
Card payment of taxAbout 2.5 percentOnline or by phone

The $150 deposit is held by the city until two years of good payment history, then credited to the account. A buyer opening service will see it, so it helps to mention it up front.

Owners here usually weigh an agent listing, a sale by owner and a sale to an investor. Since the city asks nothing of a seller for an owner-occupied sale, the real differences are time, cost and the condition of the house.

  • Agent listing. Ask for the commission rate in writing, plus an estimate of repair and staging costs.
  • Sale by owner. You set the price and run the showings. A title company still handles the closing.
  • Investor offer. An investor may take the house as it stands. One who plans to rent it must pass the $50 occupancy inspection before a tenant moves in.

Whichever route you take, find out what you owe first. A mortgage, a home equity line or unpaid property tax is paid from the sale proceeds, so ask each lender for a payoff statement before you compare offers.

sections.h2: Property tax: who bills it and how to pay
sections.html:
St. Charles County bills property tax for Wentzville. The Collector of Revenue's office is at 201 N. Second Street, Suite 134, in St. Charles, and the phone is 636-949-7470. Partial payments start at $20, though a partial payment will not keep a property out of the tax certificate sale.

  • E-check payments online or by phone carry a $1.50 fee, and cards cost about 2.5 percent.
  • Mailed payments count on the USPS postmark date. A payment mailed on December 31 may not be postmarked until the next business day.
  • Bank bill-pay should start at least five working days before December 31, because the county counts the day it receives the money.

Start with an informal hearing at the Assessor's Office. Hearings run from late April to early June, and outside a reassessment year the number to call is 636-949-7428. If you still disagree, the next level is the Board of Equalization. Its form is due by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July each year.

The last level is the Missouri State Tax Commission, with a filing date of September 30 or 30 days after the Board decision, whichever falls later. Property bought after the second Monday in June gets until December 31. Full instructions are printed on the assessment notice you receive, so keep it handy when you call.

An unpaid county bill does not block a sale. The balance is paid out of your proceeds at closing, and the title company will ask the Collector for the amount. Clear it sooner if you can, because a partial payment does not protect the parcel from the tax certificate sale. Call the Collector's office for a current figure before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
First pull together the numbers a buyer will ask for: your loan payoff, the newest county tax bill, any HOA dues and a list of recent repairs. Then decide how much cleaning and fixing you want to pay for before showing the house.

To avoid a long listing period, collect written investor offers and set each one against a realistic list price minus agent fees, repairs and carrying costs. Read who pays closing costs and what happens if the buyer backs out.

A cash sale to an investor skips the showings, the repair negotiations and most of the waiting on a buyer's loan, but it only makes sense if the net figure beats what a listing would leave you after fees and repairs.

Once you accept an offer, a title company searches for liens and prepares the settlement statement. Your mortgage payoff, any home equity line and any unpaid tax come out of the proceeds, and the remainder goes to you. Wentzville adds no city sale paperwork for an owner-occupied home, so the closing itself looks like it would in any other St. Charles County town.

If the buyer will rent the house afterward, the occupancy inspection is theirs to schedule, but it helps if you leave the house accessible and utilities on so an inspector can walk through. For a buyer who is moving in, the main city task is opening the water, trash and sewer account, which is where the deposit comes in.

Bring the title company your photo ID, the loan account number and the latest tax statement. Ask what time keys and garage openers must be handed over and whether the buyer will want a final walk-through the day before.

faqs.q: Does Wentzville inspect a house before it is sold?
faqs.a: No. The city requires no occupancy inspection when a house is sold. An inspection applies only when the house will be leased or rented to a new tenant.

faqs.q: How much is the Wentzville occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: It costs $50 and is valid for 90 days. You request it through the SmartGov permit portal, and scheduling usually takes one to two business days after payment.

faqs.q: Which county bills Wentzville property tax?
faqs.a: St. Charles County does. The Collector of Revenue is at 201 N. Second Street, Suite 134, in St. Charles, and can be reached at 636-949-7470.

faqs.q: When is the assessment appeal deadline in Wentzville?
faqs.a: The Board of Equalization form is due by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July each year. A later State Tax Commission appeal generally needs a Board filing first, unless the property was newly purchased.

faqs.q: How big is the Wentzville market?
faqs.a: About 49,495 people live in Wentzville, up from 44,372 in 2020, in western St. Charles County. Owners live in 82.5% of homes.
